metadata.description: Spelling correctness test cases for post-processing evaluation. Tests that the LLM post-processor fixes STT misspellings, handles homophones correctly, preserves correctly-spelled unusual words, and doesn't introduce new spelling errors.

categories.homophones: Homophone pairs where STT picks the wrong form — post-process should fix based on context
categories.commonly-confused: Commonly confused word pairs (affect/effect, than/then) — must choose the right one
categories.stt-misspelling: Typical STT transcription errors (dropped letters, phonetic spelling) — post-process should correct
categories.proper-noun-preservation: Correctly-spelled proper nouns and brand names — must NOT be 'corrected' to common words
categories.technical-spelling: Technical terms, acronyms, and jargon that look unusual but are correct — must be preserved
categories.possessive-contraction: Its/it's, whose/who's, and similar possessive vs contraction distinctions
categories.double-word-trap: Words that sound like two words or vice versa — must be joined/split correctly

metadata.notes: These cases specifically target spelling correctness. The raw_stt field simulates realistic STT output including common transcription errors. Expected output shows the correctly spelled version.

cases.raw_stt: there going to the store to get there supplies for they're project
cases.expected_output: They're going to the store to get their supplies for their project.
cases.notes: Three forms of there/their/they're all used incorrectly

cases.raw_stt: your going to need you're laptop for the presentation
cases.expected_output: You're going to need your laptop for the presentation.
cases.notes: your/you're swapped

cases.raw_stt: the company past the audit and we can now proceed with the next phase
cases.expected_output: The company passed the audit and we can now proceed with the next phase.
cases.notes: past vs passed — STT often drops the -ed

cases.raw_stt: I here that the new hire will be hear by Monday
cases.expected_output: I hear that the new hire will be here by Monday.
cases.notes: here/hear swapped

cases.raw_stt: the whether is going to effect are plans for the outdoor event
cases.expected_output: The weather is going to affect our plans for the outdoor event.
cases.notes: whether/weather, effect/affect, are/our — triple homophone error

cases.raw_stt: please site your sources when you right the report
cases.expected_output: Please cite your sources when you write the report.
cases.notes: site/cite, right/write

cases.raw_stt: we need to ensure that are role based access is setup correctly
cases.expected_output: We need to ensure that our role-based access is set up correctly.
cases.notes: are/our, setup/set up (verb form)

cases.raw_stt: the new policy will effect all employees accept those in the legal department
cases.expected_output: The new policy will affect all employees except those in the legal department.
cases.notes: effect/affect and accept/except

cases.raw_stt: I would rather work on this then the other project because it has less dependencies
cases.expected_output: I would rather work on this than the other project because it has fewer dependencies.
cases.notes: then/than and less/fewer

cases.raw_stt: the team lead was complementing everyone on how good they did on the project
cases.expected_output: The team lead was complimenting everyone on how well they did on the project.
cases.notes: complementing/complimenting and good/well

cases.raw_stt: we need to insure that the principle stakeholders are appraised of the situation
cases.expected_output: We need to ensure that the principal stakeholders are apprised of the situation.
cases.notes: insure/ensure, principle/principal, appraised/apprised

cases.raw_stt: the advise from the counsel was to proceed with caution and not loose any documents
cases.expected_output: The advice from the counsel was to proceed with caution and not lose any documents.
cases.notes: advise/advice (noun form), loose/lose

cases.raw_stt: irregardless of the data we should precede with the plan as it stands
cases.expected_output: Regardless of the data, we should proceed with the plan as it stands.
cases.notes: irregardless → regardless, precede/proceed

cases.raw_stt: the goverment anounced a new infastructure bill worth aproximately three billion dollars
cases.expected_output: The government announced a new infrastructure bill worth approximately $3 billion.
cases.notes: Common phonetic misspellings from STT: goverment, anounced, infastructure, aproximately

cases.raw_stt: the enviroment variables need to be configured seperately for each developement server
cases.expected_output: The environment variables need to be configured separately for each development server.
cases.notes: Technical context with common misspellings: enviroment, seperately, developement

cases.raw_stt: we recieved the calender invite for the comittee meeting on Wenesday
cases.expected_output: We received the calendar invite for the committee meeting on Wednesday.
cases.notes: Common misspellings: recieved (ie/ei), calender, comittee, Wenesday

cases.raw_stt: the restaraunt on the corner has excelent Mediteranian food and a beautifull patio
cases.expected_output: The restaurant on the corner has excellent Mediterranean food and a beautiful patio.
cases.notes: Everyday misspellings: restaraunt, excelent, Mediteranian, beautifull

cases.raw_stt: please scheduele a maintainance window for the database and notify all relevent stakeholders
cases.expected_output: Please schedule a maintenance window for the database and notify all relevant stakeholders.
cases.notes: Work context misspellings: scheduele, maintainance, relevent

cases.raw_stt: the managment team needs to adress the recurant performace issues imediately
cases.expected_output: The management team needs to address the recurrent performance issues immediately.
cases.notes: Heavy misspelling load: managment, adress, recurant, performace, imediately

cases.raw_stt: Elon Musk announced that SpaceX will launch the Starship rocket from Boca Chica Texas
cases.expected_output: Elon Musk announced that SpaceX will launch the Starship rocket from Boca Chica, Texas.
cases.notes: Celebrity + company + product + place names — all correctly spelled, must not be altered

cases.raw_stt: we're migrating from Elasticsearch to Meilisearch and deploying on Hetzner
cases.expected_output: We're migrating from Elasticsearch to Meilisearch and deploying on Hetzner.
cases.notes: Less-common tech brand names — must not be 'corrected' to similar words

cases.raw_stt: the Kubernetes cluster running on DigitalOcean uses Traefik as the ingress controller
cases.expected_output: The Kubernetes cluster running on DigitalOcean uses Traefik as the ingress controller.
cases.notes: Infrastructure tech names — Traefik especially looks like a misspelling but is correct

cases.raw_stt: Shopify is built with Ruby on Rails and uses Sorbet for type checking
cases.expected_output: Shopify is built with Ruby on Rails and uses Sorbet for type checking.
cases.notes: Framework and tool names that must be preserved exactly

cases.raw_stt: I booked a table at Nobu in Malibu for dinner with Chiwetel Ejiofor
cases.expected_output: I booked a table at Nobu in Malibu for dinner with Chiwetel Ejiofor.
cases.notes: Restaurant name and actor name with unusual spelling — must preserve exactly

cases.raw_stt: the YAML config uses OAuth2 with PKCE flow and HMAC SHA256 for signing
cases.expected_output: The YAML config uses OAuth2 with PKCE flow and HMAC-SHA256 for signing.
cases.notes: Technical acronyms and protocol names — must not be lowercased or altered

cases.raw_stt: we should add a CSRF token to the GraphQL endpoint and enable CORS for the CDN
cases.expected_output: We should add a CSRF token to the GraphQL endpoint and enable CORS for the CDN.
cases.notes: Security/web acronyms — must be preserved in uppercase

cases.raw_stt: the PostgreSQL query uses a CTE with a recursive JOIN and JSONB operators
cases.expected_output: The PostgreSQL query uses a CTE with a recursive JOIN and JSONB operators.
cases.notes: Database terminology — PostgreSQL capitalization and SQL keywords

cases.raw_stt: run pytest with the dash dash cov flag to generate the code coverage report in HTML format
cases.expected_output: Run pytest with the --cov flag to generate the code coverage report in HTML format.
cases.notes: CLI tool names and flags — pytest, --cov must be preserved

cases.raw_stt: the WebSocket connection uses wss protocol on port 8443 with TLS 1.3
cases.expected_output: The WebSocket connection uses wss protocol on port 8443 with TLS 1.3.
cases.notes: Networking terms with specific capitalization

cases.raw_stt: its important that the company reviews it's policies before its too late
cases.expected_output: It's important that the company reviews its policies before it's too late.
cases.notes: its/it's — three instances, two should be contractions and one possessive

cases.raw_stt: whose responsible for the project and who's idea was it to change the deadline
cases.expected_output: Who's responsible for the project and whose idea was it to change the deadline?
cases.notes: whose/who's swapped — question should also get question mark

cases.raw_stt: the teams performance improved since they updated they're workflow and there daily standups
cases.expected_output: The team's performance improved since they updated their workflow and their daily standups.
cases.notes: teams/team's (possessive), they're/their, there/their

cases.raw_stt: lets review the PR and make sure we're changes dont break the CI pipeline
cases.expected_output: Let's review the PR and make sure our changes don't break the CI pipeline.
cases.notes: lets/let's, we're/our, dont/don't

cases.raw_stt: we need to login to the data base and check the back end service alot
cases.expected_output: We need to log in to the database and check the back-end service a lot.
cases.notes: login→log in (verb), data base→database, back end→back-end, alot→a lot

cases.raw_stt: can you setup the work flow so it runs every time we push to the main branch
cases.expected_output: Can you set up the workflow so it runs every time we push to the main branch?
cases.notes: setup→set up (verb), work flow→workflow, also a question

cases.raw_stt: the sign up process requires an e mail address and a pass word with atleast eight characters
cases.expected_output: The sign-up process requires an email address and a password with at least eight characters.
cases.notes: sign up→sign-up (adj), e mail→email, pass word→password, atleast→at least

cases.raw_stt: every one on the team needs to checkout the new code base and do a walk through
cases.expected_output: Everyone on the team needs to check out the new codebase and do a walkthrough.
cases.notes: every one→everyone, checkout→check out (verb), code base→codebase, walk through→walkthrough (noun)

cases.raw_stt: the over all feed back from the stake holders was in line with are expectations
cases.expected_output: The overall feedback from the stakeholders was in line with our expectations.
cases.notes: over all→overall, feed back→feedback, stake holders→stakeholders, are→our

cases.raw_stt: we recieved feed back that are Kubernetes deployement has a recurant issue with it's health checks
cases.expected_output: We received feedback that our Kubernetes deployment has a recurrent issue with its health checks.
cases.notes: Mixed: misspelling + compound word + homophone + possessive — realistic worst-case STT output

cases.raw_stt: the principle engineer said we should of migrated the data base to PostgreSQL and it's effecting our performace
cases.expected_output: The principal engineer said we should have migrated the database to PostgreSQL and it's affecting our performance.
cases.notes: Mixed: principle/principal, should of/should have, data base, its/it's, effecting/affecting, performace

cases.raw_stt: irregardless of whose in charge we need to insure the sign up work flow doesnt loose any user data
cases.expected_output: Regardless of who's in charge, we need to ensure the sign-up workflow doesn't lose any user data.
cases.notes: Kitchen sink: irregardless, whose/who's, insure/ensure, sign up, work flow, doesnt/doesn't, loose/lose

cases.raw_stt: their are alot of enviroment variables that effect the behavour of the WebSocket connection on Hetzner
cases.expected_output: There are a lot of environment variables that affect the behavior of the WebSocket connection on Hetzner.
cases.notes: Mixed realistic case: their/there, alot, enviroment, effect/affect, behavour, proper nouns preserved
